@ c: the events of e tick the call, and its output has them (once each: the tick of its own n gives nothing more)
@ d: the callee that gives out at each tick of the period makes the events, and its input has them the same frame after the stage of the callee
@ g: the part that gives out only when it reads a value that is not 0 reads 0 for ever, and gives nothing
@ half in the loop: gives out at the frames of the grid of two, the last value of g between
@ a value of a parameter kind only is given out at each frame of the period of the flow, whatever m has
@ a callee that gives only None gives nothing: the output is the default (0) for ever
@ fwd of a call that is ticked by e: the events are the ones of e, and the n that is ticked by d gives nothing
@ the same part in two calls that are ticked from outside: each has the events of e with its own step
@ the same wrapping flow in three calls and two levels is not a loop: the events of e go through, each level adding its step
@ a call that gives at each tick of the period between the two calls of a loop: the two have events of their own every frame
@ a when~ that holds the part by the level of its own event: the condition has no event at first, the part does not run, and nothing is given out
@ a reset_if~ with the condition of its own event that is never true: the events of the sum are given out as with none
@ four runs of echo in a flow around them: the four events are given after the four runs, and each is received before the next
@ the same with the call that has the four runs of an up~: each event is received after its run, before the next
